summary: In February 2024 Google paused Gemini's generation of images of people after it produced inaccurate and offensive results. Senior vice president Prabhakar Raghavan said tuning meant to show a range of people failed to account for cases where a range should not be shown, and the model became over-cautious.

overview.background: Gemini (formerly Bard) could generate images. Google tuned it to avoid biased results such as one ethnicity dominating.
overview.impact: Users saw historically inaccurate and offensive results, and some reasonable prompts were refused.
overview.severity: A product pause for the people-image feature.
overview.gaps: This file uses a news analysis, Maginative, of Raghavan's post (the card source was not read).

timeline.e: Google tunes the image generator to avoid biased results.
Users post inaccurate and offensive images from Gemini.
Google acknowledges the results are embarrassing and wrong.

timeline.t: Earlier in the week of 23 Feb

timeline.e: Google commits to significant testing before re-enabling the feature.

rootCause.trigger: Tuning aimed at showing diversity did not account for cases that should not show a range.
rootCause.underlying: The model became over-cautious and treated very anodyne prompts as sensitive.

evidence.label: Over-caution
evidence.body: wrongly interpret some very anodyne prompts as sensitive
evidence.note: Raghavan's wording as quoted in the Maginative article.

evidence.label: A simulated test matrix
evidence.body:
prompt_type: specific_person_or_period | open_group | sensitive_topic
expect: faithful | varied | careful refusal
evidence.note: An illustration of how to organise tests. Not Google's.

diagnose.step: Collect failing prompts and group them.
Check refusal rates on anodyne prompts.

prevent.why: Raghavan said he cannot promise perfection.

fix.safety: A pause is a safe fallback. Prefer pausing a feature to leaving it on while fixing.

troubleshoot.scenario: Your image generator gives historically wrong results and refuses harmless prompts after a tuning change.
troubleshoot.question: What do you do?
troubleshoot.answer: Pause the affected feature, build an evaluation set covering both failure modes, retune and relaunch in stages without promising perfection.

remediation.answer: Cover specific, open and sensitive prompts.

design.prompt: Design image generation guardrails that avoid both bias and distortion.
design.answer: Context-aware rules, evaluation across prompt types, human review and staged rollout.

checks.q: What did Raghavan say he could not promise?
options: That Gemini would never produce embarrassing results
